title: Larry on patrol with a captured prisoner
description: Larry, in duck-hunter camouflage, crouches low in dense jungle looking back over his shoulder into the lens — an unposed frame taken by Captain Kennedy with his Nikon F. Close behind Larry crouches a prisoner the patrol had captured — a Pathet Lao, in Larry's telling, later turned over to the CIA. The blurred face further back is a "striker" — a strike-force irregular; 70% of the strikers, Larry says, were enemy.
larrysRecollection:
Picture of my father.
Picture taken by Captain Kennedy with his Nikon F
Person next to my father is a prisoner they captured, who is a pasthic Lao that was turned over to the CIA.

Person face in the back that is blurred is a “striker “. 70% off strikers were enemy.

Captain Kennedy sent his pictures to Hawaii to develop and when he got them back, my father took a picture of his picture

Canon Dial 35 is the camera my father purchased
researchNotes: Relayed by Larry's son from Larry's dictation (2026-08-15 session; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0023-c18035445.json, -c18035515.json, and -c18035521.json). Unusual provenance: a photograph of Captain Kennedy's print (developed in Hawaii) — which both explains any generational quality loss and firmly places Kennedy on patrol with Larry, strengthening the tentative VN-0006 identification. 'Pasthic Lao' is read as Pathet Lao; a Pathet Lao prisoner taken near Tây Ninh (far from Laos) and handed to the CIA would be a remarkable, potentially documentable event — treated as a lead. The '70% of strikers were enemy' assessment echoes documented CIDG infiltration concerns. Larry's own camera was a Canon Dial 35, bought at the Qui Nhơn PX (VN-0016 comment).
